adamw.name: AdamW
adamw.definition: An adaptive moment optimizer that applies weight decay separately from the gradient moment update.
adamw.explanation: AdamW tracks exponential averages of gradients and squared gradients, corrects their initialization bias, and divides the first by the square root of the second. It then adds λθ as a separate decay contribution. This separation matters because placing an L2 penalty inside the gradient lets Adam's adaptive scaling alter it. A resumable run stores both moment vectors, step, and all hyperparameters. Parameter-group policies may exclude gains or biases, but such choices must be explicit.

gradient-accumulation.name: gradient accumulation
gradient-accumulation.definition: Summing or averaging gradients from sequential microbatches before one optimizer update.
gradient-accumulation.explanation: Accumulation increases effective batch tokens without retaining all microbatch activations at once. Each microbatch evaluates the same unchanged parameters; only after its gradients are combined does the optimizer step. Chapter 38's public method gives every microbatch one shared target-token count, so their mean gradients receive equal weight. An unequal-size extension must instead weight each mean by its target-token count. Clipping operates on the combined global vector. Accumulation reduces activation pressure but does not reduce model, gradient, or optimizer-state storage.
